issue.title: auxiliary inventory: every request says what it is for, a dead role goes, and the prefix gate weighs the real belt (review needed)

repository.name: CodeAF
repository.description: Open-Source Software factory for Open Models

issue.body:
Three findings from an audit of this build's auxiliary machinery. All three are
things the code reports about itself incorrectly; none changes what any model is
asked or answers.

## 1. `RoleCompaction` was a priced dial wired to nothing

`Agent.compact` takes `_ context.Context` and makes no model call — a compaction
is two mechanical rearrangements of text the session already has, and the
summariser was deleted long ago. `RoleCompaction` survived it: a constant, a
`TierHigh` assignment, a description, and a row on the Providers tab offering a
person a model for a call that never happens. `TierHigh`'s own five-minute
patience was derived from "a compaction summary over a full window".

Deleted, with the settings and manual text that offered it, and the patience
re-derived from the auditor — the call on that tier that really does read a
great deal before it writes.

## 2. Nine of eleven callers of this package's model door reached the wire anonymously

The guardian, vision, the shaper, the spell-out, the subharness intake, the run
planner, the harness designer, the ceiling's handoff draft and a saved program's
own AI step all called `completeWithModel` with no `provider.WithCallTag`
anywhere above them. 2,309 of the 2,839 untagged finishes in the ten days to
2026-09-10 are this package's, and with them the answer to "what was this build
spending that model on all night".

The tag was a context value a caller could forget, and forgetting it is silent.
It is an argument now — `callPurpose` — so a call with no purpose does not
compile, and the door is the only thing in the package that calls
`provider.WithCallTag` (the turn, the ask tool and the errand ladder each used
to stamp their own).

`auxiliary.go`'s claim that `callRole` is "the one door all auxiliary provider
calls pass through" was the false one, and now says what is true: it is the one
door every **errand** passes through, and it names what is legitimately not an
errand and why.

`nohiddenwork_test.go` is the law and it is on the laws gate: a blank purpose
fails the build, a `WithCallTag` outside the door fails the build, and the walk
fails if it stops finding the door at all.

## 3. The prefix gate weighed a belt nobody runs

`fixedPrefixBudget`'s doc comment has always said it bounds "the belt the
shipping conversation door assembles". The fixture under it had no memory store,
no accounts hub, no standing items and no saved programs: 18 tools, 39,073
bytes, green with eight kilobytes to spare. A configured machine carries 23 and
weighs **53,025** — 5,025 over the 48,000 cap the gate was enforcing. Invisibly,
every day. Same shape as #576.

The gate now weighs the belt shape named `shippedBeltShape`, the same "fully
wired" definition `prompt_belt_test.go` uses, through one shared helper, and
both arms — fixed and lean — weigh the shipped shape rather than a thin fixture. The figure becomes a
ratchet at the measurement with no headroom, 48,000 stays as the stated target,
and the test prints the shortfall on every green run.

**The 5 KB is filed, not fixed:** `stand` alone is 9,607 bytes, more than a
quarter of the tool block and nearly twice the next heaviest. Trimming a schema
changes what the model is told, not a byte count, so it belongs to whoever owns
the standing belt.

## Seams reported, not worked around

- **Three roads build their own `provider.NewClient`** — the standing sentinel,
  the memory tidy-up and the document reader — and never touch this door, so
  they are outside the errand ladder. They have no `*Agent` to reach it through.
  They are no longer outside the PURPOSE law: it now requires `withPurpose` on
  every own-client completion, per call, and the negative was planted on the
  Spark (each of the three stripped in turn, each failing by file:line).
- **Four of the nine are genuine errands** — guardian, shaper, spell-out, intake
  — that could go through `callRole` and gain the ladder's fall-through, the
  tier's patience and a journal row. That asks a second model on failure, which
  is a behaviour change and does not belong in a fix PR.
- **`subharness_intake` builds its window on `context.Background()`**, so a
  person's interrupt does not cut it. Fixing it is part of the `callRole`
  conversion above.

## What this PR deliberately does not do — issue #1010

An altitude review found the shape is one level too shallow in three places, and
all three are cross-package. They are filed as **#1010**, with **#928 as the
spine**, and they mostly DELETE what this PR adds:

1. **The purpose belongs on the wire, not in a package convention.** This PR's
   law can only see `internal/session`; five other packages reach a model by
   other roads. `provider.NewClient` taking the purpose, and `calllog.Record`
   refusing an untagged row, deletes `withPurpose`, `purposeInherited` and the
   own-client second pass entirely, and makes the law one sentence module-wide.
2. **#928: `lane.Role` rides on the record.** `cmd/aforge-replay`'s `roleOf`
   table is a hand-maintained join this PR had to grow by four rows and correct
   twice. `provider.WithCallRole` beside `WithCallTag` deletes the table — and
   with it the one rename this PR carries, `purposeSentinel = "standing-check"`,
   which moves a word collision rather than fixing it.
3. **The prefix variance is removed, not measured around.** `widestBelt`,
   `bare.WidestGrepDescription` and the two normalisations in
   `prefixbudget_test.go` exist only because `grep` and `load_capability` say
   different sentences on different machines (169 bytes). One description
   everywhere with the machine fact delivered at runtime deletes all of that.
   That one needs the belt's owner: `bare`'s stated law says the opposite.

Both holding actions now name #1010 where a reader meets them
(`clientdoor.go`'s `purposeSentinel`, `prefixbudget_test.go`'s residue note).

## Proof

- `go build ./... && go vet ./...` clean.
- Laws, manual, roles, session, tui3 and cmd suites on the Spark (see comment).
- Real-model run on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` checking `calls.jsonl` has a
  role on every auxiliary row and none untagged (see comment).

issue.title: The prefix budget measures a quantity that changes with what is installed on the machine: grep's description is 134 bytes longer without ripgrep

milestone.title: Reliable agent

repository.name: CodeAF
repository.description: Open-Source Software factory for Open Models

issue.body:
## Symptom

`TestTheLeanPrefixStaysUnderItsBudget` reads a different number on every machine at the same commit. Measured at `d84120b30`'s parent shape, one sha, three boxes:

| where | lean prefix | tool block |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub runner (`touched packages`) | 31,555 | 14,390 |
| this laptop | 31,484 | 14,319 |
| the Spark | 31,453 | — |

The gate failed on CI while passing on both machines the lane could run it on, which is the worst shape a budget can have: the lane cutting bytes cannot see the number the gate will read.

## Cause

`internal/exec/bare/grepfindls.go`. `ripgrepPath` probes `exec.LookPath("rg")` once per process and `grepToolDescription` picks the description from it — `grepDescription` where ripgrep is installed, `grepFallbackDescription` where it is not, and the fallback carries two extra sentences ("Walks the tree itself (ripgrep is not on this machine), so it does NOT read .gitignore — it skips .git, node_modules, vendor and files that look binary"). The GitHub runner has no `rg`; this laptop has one at `/opt/homebrew/bin/rg`.

That is **134 bytes** of difference in one tool, and it lands in the tool block the budget weighs.

The behaviour itself is right and was deliberate (#: "A CAPABILITY THAT CANNOT WORK IS ABSENT, AND THIS ONE CAN ALWAYS WORK" — the tool keeps its name and only its engine and one sentence change). What is wrong is that a LEDGER measures it.

## Replication — a stranger can run this

```sh
git checkout <any commit on dev>
go test -run TestTheLeanPrefixStaysUnderItsBudget -v ./internal/session   # with rg on PATH
env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:$(dirname $(which go)) \
  go test -run TestTheLeanPrefixStaysUnderItsBudget -v ./internal/session # with rg hidden
```

On `dev` at `84016ad09` those two read **31,341** and **31,448**: a 107-byte spread with nothing changed but `PATH`. The second figure is the one CI reads.

## Acceptance

The budget test measures a figure that does not move with the machine, and says which shape it measured. Either:

- it weighs the belt with the probe pinned to a stated answer (both arms, or the worst arm), and the failure message names the arm; or
- the environment-dependent sentence leaves the description and becomes a fact the tool answers with, so the description is one string everywhere.

Either way, `internal/session/prefixbudget_test.go` fails identically on the laptop, the Spark and the GitHub runner at one sha, and a lane that measures 40 bytes of headroom has 40 bytes of headroom.

Found while cutting #923's prefix cost: that PR read 18 bytes under the budget on the laptop and 55 over on CI, and the difference was entirely this.

issue.title: calls.jsonl records the call site's tag but not the lane.Role it was routed under, so a watched task step and an unwatched one are the same row

milestone.title: Reliable agent
milestone.description: Tasks, spend/routing, and headless endings behave as claimed — checks, worktrees, receipts, model ladders, and spend that match reality.

repository.name: CodeAF
repository.description: Open-Source Software factory for Open Models

issue.body:
## What is wrong

`calllog.Record` — the row every model call writes to `~/.aforge/logs/calls.jsonl` —
carries a `tag` (the call site's own word for the errand) and does **not** carry the
[`lane.Role`](../blob/dev/internal/lane/roles.go) the call was actually routed under.

The role is the thing that decides how the call was routed: λ, the quality bar, the
exploration horizon and — the one a person feels — `Visible`, which is the whole of the
watched/unattended split. It is in the context at the moment of the call
(`provider.WithRole`), and it is dropped on the floor before the row is written.

So anything that reads the log back has to reconstruct it, and reconstruction is lossy
in a way that cannot be repaired from the file:

- `RoleLeafAttached` and `RoleLeafUnattended` write the **same** tag, `task`.
  `internal/session`'s `laneRole` asks `someoneIsWatching()` at the moment of the call and
  nothing records the answer. A watched task step and an unwatched one are
  indistinguishable in the log, and they differ in exactly the field that decides whether
  a person's seconds were being spent.
- The tag vocabularies do not line up. `internal/session/auxiliary.go` writes
  `string(role)` for an `internal/roles.Role`; `cmd/aforge/chat.go`'s `errandContext`
  writes the errand's *name* (`title`, `distill`, `quorum`, `craft-params`, …);
  `internal/session/toolask.go` writes `tool:<tool>`. Three vocabularies, one column,
  and the `lane.Role` that all three already had in hand is in none of them.

## Replication

A stranger can run this with no private data:

```sh
go test ./cmd/aforge-replay/ -run TestEveryTagTheBuildWritesResolvesToARoleSomebodyDeclared -v
```

That law walks the tree for every tag the build can write and fails on one the replay's
`callSiteRoles` table does not name — it is the stopgap standing in for the missing
column, and it exists only because the column is missing. Delete a row from
`cmd/aforge-replay/request.go`'s `callSiteRoles` and it goes red, naming the tag.

The join itself is `roleOf` in `cmd/aforge-replay/request.go`, whose doc comment says it
is "the first thing to delete when the role reaches the row".

## Acceptance

End-to-end, through the door the product uses:

1. `calllog.Record` gains a `role` column (`json:"role,omitempty"`), filled from the call
   context the same way `tag` is (`internal/provider/calllog.go`'s `callTag`, beside it).
2. An untagged test drives a real call through `internal/provider` with
   `provider.WithRole(ctx, lane.RoleLeafAttached)` and asserts the written JSON line
   carries `"role":"leaf.attached"` — not `leaf.unattended`, which is the reading every
   reader of the log is forced into today.
3. `cmd/aforge-replay`'s `roleOf` and its whole `callSiteRoles` table are **deleted**, and
   `TestEveryTagTheBuildWritesResolvesToARoleSomebodyDeclared` with them; the replay reads
   `row.Role` directly. A mixed log (ten days of rows with no `role`) still replays — the
   old rows read as `RoleUnknown` and the report says how many.

## Why it matters now

`cmd/aforge-replay` (#922) reports mean regret per role class over the real log, and the
watched half of that table is built on this guess. Its `task` numbers are a **floor** on
how bad a watched task step was and can never be a ceiling, and the report has to say so
instead of printing a number.

## Evidence

PR #922, `cmd/aforge-replay/request.go` `roleOf` / `callSiteRoles`;
`internal/calllog/calllog.go:125` (the `tag` field's own comment);
`internal/session/auxiliary.go:196`; `cmd/aforge/chat.go:5795`;
`internal/session/toolask.go:121`; `docs/design/recovery/census-20260910.md` §8 finding 9,
which is the last time the missing tag cost somebody an answer.

repository.name: CodeAF
repository.description: Open-Source Software factory for Open Models

issue.body:
## Why

#996 closed the auxiliary inventory one package deep. Its review (five passes, 2026-09-12) found the shape stops short in three places that are each a cross-package change and belong together as one wave, with #928 as the spine:

1. **Purpose is a precondition of the wire, not a package convention.** `provider.NewClient` (or the one place `calllog.Record` is written) takes the purpose and refuses/loudly flags an anonymous row. Deletes `withPurpose`, the inherited-blank exemption, the own-client second pass in `internal/session`, and covers `internal/reflex`, `internal/head`, `internal/exec`, `internal/revision`, `internal/plan` and `cmd/aforge`, which today spell `provider.WithCallTag` by hand and are invisible to `internal/session`'s package-local law. The law becomes "no `provider.NewClient` outside the dispatcher without a purpose", module-wide.
2. **`lane.Role` rides on the record** (`provider.WithCallRole` beside `WithCallTag`), so `cmd/aforge-replay`'s `roleOf` table is deleted rather than grown, the `vision`/`spellout` rows stop being hand-priced, and the standing check's tag reverts from `standing-check` to its role's own word `sentinel` (three packages spell "sentinel" for three things today; the join fixes that, not a rename).
3. **Remove the prefix variance instead of measuring around it**: one `grep` description everywhere (the "ripgrep absent" fact delivered at runtime in the tool result or one caps line), `load_capability` names what the build COULD have, so the fixed prefix is one number on every machine and `widestBelt` / `WidestGrepDescription` / the members seam in `internal/exec/bare` are deleted. Owner of `bare`'s grep-description law must be in the room: that file states the two facts must be told up front.

## Acceptance

End-to-end first: `aforge chat --once` on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` with the guard, then `~/.aforge/logs/calls.jsonl` shows every row with a purpose AND a lane role, including rows from the resident's quorum errand and a reflex call; `cmd/aforge-replay` prices them with no table. Unit: the module-wide go/ast law; the prefix gate's number identical on macOS with ripgrep+ffmpeg and on the Linux runner without either.

Measurements that make the case are in #996's PR body and `PERF.md`'s prefix section.

issue.body:
The spend a conversation reports is the spend the provider actually saw. Routing pins what it claims to pin, and the record names the machine that answered.

Behind this card: #1029, #1010.

👍 this issue if it matters to you. Reactions inform sequencing; they are not commitments.
